Subject: POC capacity planning & next steps — ACME AI

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed plan so we have a single source of truth for the POC.

Scope of POC (2 weeks)
- Goal: Validate Redwood Dedicated for ACME AI model serving (chat & long-form generation) against latency/throughput & cost targets.
- Success criteria (what ACME asked to validate):
  - Latency: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 600ms for conversational prompts (average length ~120 tokens).
  - Throughput: support steady-state 40 QPS with spikes to 120 QPS for up to 15 minutes.
  - Quality: no regressions vs current baseline on the ACME test set (we'll run eval suite).
  - Cost: baseline unit cost within 20% of current infra (we'll report per-1M-token estimate).

Evaluation plan
- Dataset: ACME will provide a 5k prompt validation set + 3 representative high-latency examples.
- Runs: baseline run (no caching, default batching) -> tuning run (batching, KV caching, quantization profile) -> burst test (simulated traffic shape).
- Monitoring: Redwood Console dashboards for per-route latency, token breakdown, and cost estimates will be shared live.

Capacity & infra suggestions (initial recommendation)
- Reserved capacity: 2 GPUs (reserved) for baseline steady-state. We'll allocate from Redwood Dedicated (customer-dedicated pool).
- Autoscaling: scale from 2 -> up to 6 GPUs for burst (2x–3x headroom). Policy: scale steps of +1 GPU with rapid scale for request concurrency; max sustained scale window 15 minutes for burst scenarios.
- Warm-up/Pre-warm: recommend pre-warm policy before business-hour spikes; cold-start to fully warmed can be 45–90s depending on model size.
- Expected per-GPU throughput (est): ~20–30 sustained QPS for long-form generation config; short-turn chat prompt throughput higher. We will validate exact numbers during baseline.

Ownership & timeline
- Marissa Cole (AE) — overall POC lead / kickoff scheduling.
- Vivek Kulkarni (SE) — capacity tuning, infra config, autoscale policy.
- Neha Kapoor (CS) — monitoring, eval tracking, and rollout checklist.
- ACME owners: Alex Chen (Product), Priya Sinha (Engineering lead).

High-level timeline
- Mar 2: kickoff & config (access, keys, datasets).
- Mar 3–5: baseline runs + initial metrics capture.
- Mar 6–9: tuning (batching, caching, autoscale thresholds).
- Mar 10: joint review & decision on final config.
- Mar 11–13: wrap up, handoff & optional extended trial if needed.

Next steps (action items)
- Alex/Priya: share validation dataset + expected traffic shape (CSV) by EOD Mon, Mar 1.
- ACME infra: confirm IP allowlist + service account for Redwood by Mar 2.
- Marissa: schedule kickoff (proposed Mon 3/2 10am PT).
- Vivek: attach capacity estimate (see attached spreadsheet) and we will refine after baseline.

Attachments: POC_MA_plan_v1.pdf (plan), acme_capacity_estimate.xlsx (initial numbers).

Thanks — happy to refine if you want different success criteria.

Best,

Hi Alex — quick answers while we refine the capacity sheet:  
- QPS per GPU: for a 70B decoder-style model in our inference profile, expect ~20–30 steady-state QPS per A100-style GPU for generation workloads at 120-token average. Shorter chat-style prompts typically get you higher QPS (35–50). We'll pin exact numbers after the baseline run.
- Scale-to-zero: Redwood Dedicated can scale down reserved + autoscale pools to 0 for non-reserved lanes, but note that reserved GPUs are billed while reserved. Scaling the serving layer to 0 increases first-request latency due to model load (warm-up). Typical warm-up to reach steady-state p95 is ~45–90s depending on model and quantization.
- Recommendation: reserve 2 GPUs (steady-state) to meet your 40 QPS SLA, and allow autoscale up to 6 GPUs for 120 QPS bursts. If you want deeper nightly cost savings, we can run a hybrid: reserve 1 GPU + autoscale with pre-warm window for business hours — this reduces cost but increases risk during unexpected spikes.

I attached an initial estimate. Also linking our infra tuning doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cPOC-capacity-doc — will add notes after baseline.

Regards,
